title: Without Mosaic ceremonies we are justified and sanctified (Galatians)
source_text: XLII. Praeterea dum Apostolus affirmat hominem justificari sine operibus legis, speciatim docere vult ad nostram coram Deo justificationem, necessarium non esse ut observemus legis Mosaicae ceremonias, sicut praesertim videre est in Epistola ad Galatas. Qua ratione quoque sine operibus legis sanctificamur. Nec enim magis necesse est nos observare legis ceremonias, ut sancti simus apud Deum, quam ut ab omni reatu in judicio illius absolvamur.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, when the Apostle affirms that a man is justified without works of the law, he wishes especially to teach that for our justification before God it is not necessary that we observe the ceremonies of the Mosaic law, as is especially to be seen in the Epistle to the Galatians. In which way we are also sanctified without works of the law. For it is no more necessary that we observe the ceremonies of the law in order to be holy before God than that we be absolved from all guilt in his judgment.
pass_b_english: Justify without works of the law especially means without Mosaic ceremonies (Galatians).
Same for sanctification: ceremonies not required to be holy before God.
